_doc: HMTc Category 13 — Cosmetics and Personal Care, LEAVE-ON. Nineteen product rows covering every dermal cosmetic form that remains on skin, hair or nails after application. The governing instrument family is sovereign FINISHED-COSMETIC contaminant limits for technically unavoidable heavy-metal impurities, expressed as total content per unit mass of the product as placed on market (ug/kg). That basis is neither dietary nor a migration or leachate value, and it is not a colour-additive or ingredient purity specification: the register's many us_fda_21cfr73_* and 21cfr74_* rows bound the purity of one raw material and are refused by every row's basis guard. The EU is not the anchor in this family. Regulation 1223/2009 Annex II prohibits lead, cadmium, arsenic, mercury, antimony, nickel and chromium(VI) compounds as intentional cosmetic ingredients but publishes no numeric ceiling for technically unavoidable traces, and Codex has no cosmetic standard, so the numbers are written by national competent authorities. The strictest general tier in the register is the German BVL 2017 orientation table (Pb 2000, Cd 100, tAs 500, tHg 100 ug/kg), which is also the instrument Category 15 already relies on; the same table writes the family's only formulation splits, raising lead to 5000 for make-up powder, rouge, eye shadow, eyeliner, kajal and theatrical make-up, and arsenic to 2500 for theatrical make-up. Korea MFDS writes the family's only nickel tiers (eye makeup 35000, colour makeup 30000, all other cosmetics 10000). Tattoo and permanent-make-up mixtures are governed by a separate instrument family, EU REACH Annex XVII entry 75 with Appendix 13, on an intradermal mixture basis. Five of the eleven panel cells have no sovereign number anywhere in this family: aluminium, tin and total chromium are unregulated for cosmetics in every jurisdiction checked, and inorganic arsenic and hexavalent chromium are unregulated for every form except tattoo mixtures. All five are controls, with total chromium carried as the screen governing the Cr(VI) reflex; only methylmercury is a not-material determination, on the speciation-bounded ground that a cosmetic matrix has no methylation pathway. The single additive-permitted determination in the category is aluminium on the antiperspirant row, where aluminium salts are the monograph active.

_category.name: Cosmetics and Personal Care — Leave-on
_category.anchor: Strictest applicable sovereign FINISHED-COSMETIC contaminant maximum for technically unavoidable heavy-metal impurities, on a total-content basis (ug/kg of product as placed on market). The general tier is anchored by the German BVL 2017 orientation table; the only formulation splits in the family are the German make-up lead and theatrical-make-up arsenic branches and the Korean MFDS nickel product-class tiers, each preserved where the government wrote it. Tattoo and permanent-make-up mixtures are anchored on EU REACH Annex XVII entry 75, Appendix 13, an intradermal mixture instrument.
_category.basis_family: finished cosmetic total content, as placed on market (ug/kg of product as sold) — never a dietary basis, never a migration or leachate basis, never an ingredient or colour-additive purity specification
_category.method_label: HMTc Method v2.0, government-limit-only initial setting: every numeric cell is the strictest applicable sovereign maximum for this exact leave-on cosmetic form expressed as total content of the finished product as placed on market, or a disclosed read-across where the exact cell is unregulated, or a substantiated not-material determination, or a control. No cell is occurrence-derived, no cell is precautionary or feasibility-adjusted, and no cell is anchored on an ingredient or colour-additive purity specification.
_category.method_note:
Five method points govern this category and each is visible in the records.

(1) The credible set is widened because the default set does not write this family. The EU bans these elements as intentional cosmetic ingredients without publishing a numeric trace ceiling, Codex has no cosmetic standard, and FSANZ does not regulate cosmetics; every numeric finished-cosmetic value in the register comes from a national or regional competent authority.

(1a) The instrument status of the binding tier is disclosed, not dressed up. The German BVL 2017 values that bind lead, cadmium, arsenic and mercury across this category are recorded in the register with status 'guidance impurity limit': they are orientation values published by the German Federal Office of Consumer Protection and Food Safety for heavy-metal contents considered technically AVOIDABLE under good manufacturing practice, operating against the EU Article 17 requirement that traces be technically unavoidable, rather than a maximum level written into a statute. HMTc adopts them because they are the strictest applicable maximum published by a national competent authority for this exact product family, and because Category 15 already rests on the same instrument. A hostile reader should be told two further things rather than discover them. First, the STATUTORY floor in this family sits well above the adopted value: China NMPA 2015 and Taiwan MOHW 2024 (lead 10000, cadmium 5000, arsenic 2000-3000, mercury 1000 ug/kg) and the US FDA 21 CFR 700.13 mercury adulteration rule (1000) are binding instruments, and every product meeting an HMTc cell in this category satisfies all of them by construction, so certification never depends on the guidance status of the German table. Second, the nickel cells rest on Korea MFDS, which IS a statutory instrument. Adopting a guidance value that is stricter than every statute in the family moves the standard toward more protection, never less, so the status question affects how the value is described and never whether a certified product is lawful.

(2) Where a taxonomy row bundles forms that a government instrument splits, the row binds at the strictest value applicable to ANY form in it, so a published ceiling is never looser than the government value for a product certified against it. That is why the makeup, body-paint and eye-makeup rows bind lead at the German general 2000 ug/kg rather than the higher 5000 make-up branch: liquid foundation, mascara, brow products, primers and fixatives are not in the higher branch and take the general value. Where EVERY form in a row falls inside a government split, the split's value binds instead — traditional eye cosmetics, whose forms are the 'kajal' the German instrument names at 5000, and the Korean nickel tiers. Over-compliance created by row aggregation is disclosed in the affected cell, never presented as a government requirement.

(3) Read-across is reached only when the exact cell is unregulated, so it is used nowhere in this category: every form here has a directly applicable general-cosmetic instrument. In particular the German dentifrice tier (lead 500 ug/kg) is NOT read across onto lip products, even though lip products are partly ingested and that is the dentifrice tier's own rationale, because the exact cell is already regulated by the general branch and stretching a toothpaste value onto a non-toothpaste form is the conflation this method forbids. The absence of any sovereign lip-specific ceiling is recorded as a standards gap.

(4) Aluminium, tin and total chromium have no sovereign cosmetic maximum in any jurisdiction checked, and inorganic arsenic and Cr(VI) have none for any form except tattoo mixtures. All are controls: testing is mandatory, escalation rules are published, and no ceiling is invented. Total chromium is the mandatory screen that governs the Cr(VI) reflex, and is not a protective standalone ceiling because cosmetic total chromium is dominated by benign Cr(III) pigments. Methylmercury is the category's only speciation-bounded not-material determination, bounded by the published total-mercury cell and reopened by reflex for any marine-, fish- or algal-derived ingredient. Cr(VI) is deliberately NOT treated as a method artifact: the EU legislated a Cr(VI) limit for tattoo mixtures precisely because the species occurs in inorganic pigments.

(5) Intentional-use allowances are permissions, not ceilings, and none is adopted: the mercurial eye-preservative carve-outs (Hong Kong and India 70 ppm, South Africa 65 ppm, New Zealand 0.007 percent), the Australian lead-acetate hair-treatment exception, and the aluminium active permission in antiperspirants. Prohibitions are enforced alongside the numbers rather than converted into them: the United States does not permit kohl as a colour additive and revoked the lead-acetate hair-dye listing, so a product with an unlawful composition in a target market cannot be certified whatever its measured values.
_category.credible_note: The default credible set (EU, UK, Codex, international, US, AU-NZ, CA, HK) does not write this instrument family. EU Regulation 1223/2009 prohibits these elements as intentional cosmetic ingredients under Annex II and permits technically unavoidable traces under Article 17 WITHOUT publishing any numeric ceiling; Codex has no cosmetic standard; FSANZ does not regulate cosmetics. Every numeric finished-cosmetic contaminant value in the register is written by a national or regional competent authority, so the set is widened to the authorities that actually publish this family: Germany (BVL 2017 orientation values — the strictest general tier in the register and the anchor Category 15 already relies on), China NMPA 2015, Health Canada, Taiwan MOHW 2024, Korea MFDS Notices 2024-9 and 2025-63 (the only cosmetic nickel and antimony tiers anywhere), the ASEAN Cosmetic Directive 2019 with its Indonesian, Malaysian, Singaporean and Thai transpositions, India's Cosmetics Rules 2020 and IS 3959:2004, Kenya KS 2937:2021, the EAEU TR CU 009/2011 natural-plant-or-mineral-raw-material tier, Hong Kong Cap. 640, New Zealand HSR002552, South Africa GN R.1227, Brazil ANVISA RDC 628/2022, Australia's 1956 customs instrument, and Washington State's Toxic-Free Cosmetics Act. Widening the set is what makes 'strictest applicable' a real constraint rather than an empty one: it is why the German 2000/100/500/100 ug/kg tier binds instead of the 20000 ug/kg ASEAN lead value, and it puts every one of these instruments inside the compiler's stricter-unselected audit scan so a missed stricter anchor surfaces in the report. Two register-status facts belong with this note. Sri Lanka SLS 187:2025, the only children's skin-powder tier in the register, and the US FDA draft cosmetic lead guidance both carry draft status and are gated out of every cell by the compiler; neither would have bound in any case, both being looser than the German values.

fragrance-preparations.name: Fragrance preparations (perfumes, colognes, body sprays)
fragrance-preparations.native_basis: finished leave-on cosmetic as placed on market — total heavy-metal content per unit mass of the product as sold (ug/kg). Total content, not a migration or leachate value, and not a dietary basis. No reconstitution, dilution, or in-use concentration conversion is applied: the ceiling is compared to the product in the form the consumer buys it.
fragrance-preparations.native_basis_label: Finished leave-on cosmetic, TOTAL CONTENT as placed on market (ug/kg of product as sold), on the technically-unavoidable-impurity basis every instrument in this family uses. Not a migration/leachate basis, not a dietary basis, not an ingredient purity specification.
fragrance-preparations.scope_note: In scope: alcoholic and hydroalcoholic fragrance concentrates, eau de parfum, eau de toilette, cologne, splash and body-spray forms, and pressurised body sprays, all of which remain on skin after application. Out of scope: rinse-off fragranced washes (Category 14), fragranced leave-on skin care (routed to the face/neck or body/hand leave-on rows), and room or fabric fragrance, which is not a cosmetic at all. The EAEU natural-raw-material tier is written for 'perfumery-cosmetic products' and does reach this row where natural plant or mineral raw material exceeds one percent, but at 5000 ug/kg lead it is looser than the binding German value and does not change the cell. Liquid and hydroalcoholic forms are adjudicated on the mass basis (ug/kg of product) that the binding German instrument uses; the volumetric alternative some instruments offer (mg/L) is not substituted for it and no density conversion is applied. Pressurised and airbrush forms: the ceiling applies to the product as placed on market, i.e. the contents of the container including propellant, tested as dispensed. A concentrate-basis laboratory result is never compared to an as-placed-on-market ceiling; where only the concentrate was analysed the basis is recorded and the lot is retested as dispensed. No invented concentrate-to-as-packed conversion factor is used anywhere in this category.
fragrance-preparations.basis_guard: ^(?!.*(color additive ingredient specification|colou?rant impurity|colourant impurity profile|colorant impurity))(?=.*(cosmetic|finished topical product)).*
fragrance-preparations.basis_guard_note: Every named anchor must sit on a FINISHED-COSMETIC (or finished topical product) total-content basis. The guard refuses two families outright. (1) Colour-additive and ingredient purity specifications: the US 21 CFR 73/74 rows, the New Zealand HSR002552 and Singapore ACD carbon-black colourant profiles, the India Cosmetics Rules permitted-colour specification and the Brazil ANVISA RDC 628/2022 organic-colorant specification all bound the purity of ONE raw material, not the maximum for the finished product. Anchoring a finished-product ceiling on a raw-material purity spec is a basis conflation and would be an audit blocker; each of them is also looser than the value that binds here. (2) The EU REACH tattoo and permanent-make-up mixture basis, which is an intradermally introduced mixture and belongs only to the tattoo-inks row. Dietary maximum levels and article migration/extraction limits fail the guard for the same reason.

Pb.label: the Washington Toxic-Free Cosmetics Act finished-cosmetic lead cap (RCW 70A.560.020, 1 ppm = 1000 ug/kg, including impurity lead), the strictest applicable sovereign finished-cosmetic lead maximum; the German BVL 2017 general-cosmetic value (2000) is retained as a disclosed looser candidate
Pb.basis_label: Finished cosmetic total content as placed on market (ug/kg of product as sold); technically-unavoidable-impurity basis. Not migration, not leachate, not dietary, not an ingredient purity specification.
Pb.substantiation: Applicable sovereign maxima surveyed for this exact form: Germany BVL 2017 general cosmetic orientation value, 2000 ug/kg; China NMPA 2015, 10000; Health Canada, 10000; Taiwan MOHW 2024, 10000; Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63, 20000; Singapore HSA 2024 and the ASEAN directive with its Indonesian and Malaysian transpositions, 20000; Kenya KS 2937:2021, 20000. Looser and therefore non-binding: the EAEU natural-raw-material tier (5000), the Korean clay-powder tier (50000), the India IS 3959:2004 skin-powder rows (20000 and 10000) and the Australian customs value (250000). The German value binds. Its own scope excludes the make-up categories the same table lists at 5000 ug/kg (make-up powder, rouge, eye shadow, eyeliner, kajal and theatrical make-up); none of those forms falls in this row, so the general branch is the applicable cell. The US FDA draft lead guidance for lip and externally applied cosmetics (10000) carries draft status in the register, is gated out by the compiler, and is looser in any case. No colour-additive or ingredient purity specification is used as an anchor: the US 21 CFR 73/74 cosmetic-use specifications (10000-20000 ug/kg), the India permitted-colour specification (20000), the Brazil ANVISA RDC 628/2022 organic-colorant specification (20000) and the New Zealand / Singapore carbon-black colourant profiles (10000) bound one raw material's purity rather than the finished product, they are refused by this row's basis guard, and every one of them is looser than the binding value in any event.

Cd.label: Strictest applicable sovereign cadmium maximum for a finished cosmetic: Germany BVL 2017 general cosmetic orientation value, 100 ug/kg.
Cd.basis_label: Finished cosmetic total content as placed on market (ug/kg of product as sold); technically-unavoidable-impurity basis. Not migration, not leachate, not dietary, not an ingredient purity specification.
Cd.substantiation: Applicable sovereign maxima surveyed for a finished cosmetic: Germany BVL 2017, 100 ug/kg; Thailand (ASEAN transposition), 3000; Health Canada, 3000; China NMPA 2015, 5000; Taiwan MOHW 2024, 5000; Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63, 5000; Singapore HSA 2024 and the ASEAN directive with its Indonesian and Malaysian transpositions, 5000. The German value binds and is 30-fold stricter than the next instrument. Germany writes NO formulation split for cadmium — unlike lead and arsenic, where the same table raises the value for named make-up categories — so the 100 ug/kg value applies to every product form in this category without exception. Sri Lanka SLS 187:2025 (children's skin powder, 3000) carries draft status in the register and is gated out by the compiler.

tAs.label: Strictest applicable sovereign total-arsenic maximum for a finished cosmetic: Germany BVL 2017 general cosmetic orientation value, 500 ug/kg.
tAs.basis_label: Finished cosmetic total content as placed on market (ug/kg of product as sold); technically-unavoidable-impurity basis. Not migration, not leachate, not dietary, not an ingredient purity specification.
tAs.substantiation: Applicable sovereign maxima surveyed: Germany BVL 2017 general cosmetic value, 500 ug/kg; China NMPA 2015, 2000; Kenya KS 2937:2021, 2000; Health Canada, 3000; Taiwan MOHW 2024, 3000; Singapore HSA 2024 and the ASEAN directive with its transpositions, 5000; EAEU natural-raw-material tier, 5000; Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63, 10000. The German value binds. The only arsenic split the German table writes raises the value to 2500 ug/kg for theatre, fan and carnival make-up, which does not reach this row. The arsenic cells in this instrument family are TOTAL arsenic; no jurisdiction publishes an inorganic-arsenic maximum for a cosmetic, which is why the iAs cell on this row is a control bounded by this total-arsenic ceiling rather than a number.

subsumed.rationale: iAs carries no product-specific sovereign cell; it is a component of and bounded by its parent total tAs (iAs <= tAs), an enforceable ceiling via reflex speciation rather than an empty cell.

tHg.substantiation: Applicable sovereign maxima surveyed: Germany BVL 2017, 100 ug/kg; US FDA 21 CFR 700.13 (a binding adulteration rule, mercury unavoidable under good manufacturing practice), 1000; China NMPA 2015, 1000; Health Canada, 1000; Taiwan MOHW 2024, 1000; Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63, 1000; Hong Kong Cap. 640, 1000; Singapore HSA 2024 and the ASEAN directive with its transpositions, 1000; Kenya KS 2937:2021, 2000; EAEU TR CU 009/2011 natural-raw-material tier, 1000. Ni.label: Korea MFDS 'other cosmetics' nickel tier, 10000 ug/kg — the strictest branch of the only cosmetic nickel instrument in the register, and the branch that covers this product form.
Ni.basis_label: Finished cosmetic total content as placed on market (ug/kg of product as sold); technically-unavoidable-impurity basis. Not migration, not leachate, not dietary, not an ingredient purity specification.
Ni.substantiation: Korea MFDS is the ONLY authority in the register that publishes a nickel maximum for a finished cosmetic, and the instrument tiers it by product class: eye makeup 35000 ug/kg, colour makeup 30000, all other cosmetics 10000. Method step 4 requires the government's own product-form split to be preserved, so the applicable branch is selected rather than the strictest branch overall. Both register transpositions of the instrument (MFDS Notice 2024-9 and Notice 2025-63) are named and carry identical values, which is the cross-edition check. No other credible authority publishes a cosmetic nickel ceiling: the EU prohibits nickel compounds as intentional cosmetic ingredients under Regulation 1223/2009 Annex II without setting a numeric trace maximum, and Germany's BVL 2017 table covers only lead, cadmium, arsenic, mercury and antimony. This row is neither an eye-makeup nor a colour-makeup product, so the 10000 ug/kg branch is the applicable cell and it binds. Where the mapping of an HMTc row onto the Korean product classes is not unambiguous, or where a row's forms straddle two branches, HMTc takes the stricter branch rather than claiming the looser one.

control.rationale: No jurisdiction publishes a tin maximum for a finished cosmetic. The register's tin values are dietary maximum levels for canned foods and powdered beverages, and skin-contact-article or food-contact organotin limits — a dietary basis and a migration basis respectively, neither of which can anchor a cosmetic total-content cell — and there is no near-neighbour cosmetic tin cell to read across from. Tin nevertheless enters this category by real routes: tin-oxide pearlescent and nail-lacquer pigments, organotin catalyst and elastomer residues, and tinplate or tin-lined packaging and closures. Testing is therefore mandatory and no ceiling is invented.
control.reference_method: Total tin by ICP-MS after microwave acid digestion, every lot, with organotin speciation by GC-ICP-MS wherever a tin-bearing pigment, catalyst or elastomer component is declared or a tin-lined pack is used. Escalation: a total-tin result above the SKU's established baseline triggers pigment, packaging and closure traceback and CAPA.

control.rationale: No jurisdiction publishes an aluminium maximum for a finished cosmetic. The register's aluminium values are a food-additive permission (China GB 2760) and a drinking-water guideline, neither of which is a cosmetic total-content basis, and there is no near-neighbour cosmetic aluminium cell to read across from. Aluminium is nonetheless present in this category at high and highly variable levels by design and by mineral origin — alumina and aluminium-hydroxide fillers and substrates, aluminium-lake pigments, kaolin, bentonite and talc, aluminium powder and aluminium salts — so a single contaminant ceiling would be meaningless while the metal itself cannot go unmeasured. Testing is therefore mandatory and no ceiling is invented.
control.reference_method: Total aluminium by ICP-OES or ICP-MS after microwave acid digestion, every lot, reported on the certificate together with the declared aluminium-bearing ingredients so that the measured burden can be reconciled against the formulation. Escalation: an aluminium result that the declared formulation cannot account for triggers raw-material traceback and CAPA, because unexplained aluminium indicates an undeclared mineral filler, which is also the most common carrier of the lead, cadmium and arsenic this row does cap.

control.rationale: No jurisdiction publishes a total-chromium maximum for a finished cosmetic. The register's total-chromium values are dietary maximum levels and article limits (toy and stationery coatings, jewellery) in bases that cannot anchor a cosmetic total-content cell, and there is no near-neighbour cosmetic total-chromium cell to read across from. Total chromium in a cosmetic is in any case dominated by benign trivalent chromium from chromium-oxide green and chromium-hydroxide green pigments and from stainless-steel processing contact, so a standalone total-chromium ceiling would not be protective even if a government published one: the health-relevant species is Cr(VI). Total chromium is therefore carried as the mandatory SCREEN that governs the Cr(VI) reflex on this row, and no ceiling is invented.
control.reference_method: Total chromium by ICP-MS after microwave acid digestion, every lot. It is the screen, not a pass/fail ceiling. A total-chromium result above the SKU's established baseline, or the declaration of any chromium-bearing pigment, mandates Cr(VI) speciation under this row's Cr-VI control. Escalation: unexplained total-chromium elevation triggers pigment and raw-material traceback and CAPA.

control.rationale: No jurisdiction publishes a hexavalent-chromium maximum for a topically applied finished cosmetic. The only Cr(VI) instrument in this instrument family is the EU tattoo and permanent-make-up restriction (REACH Annex XVII entry 75, Appendix 13, 500 ug/kg), which governs a mixture introduced INTRADERMALLY, not a dermal cosmetic; reading it across would substitute one exposure route and one instrument family for another, which is the stretch this method forbids. The remaining sovereign Cr(VI) values in the register are article extraction limits for textiles and leather, a migration basis that cannot anchor a total-content cell. A not-material determination is NOT available here: Cr(VI) in a pigmented cosmetic matrix is not a method artifact, and the EU legislated a Cr(VI) limit for tattoo mixtures precisely because the species occurs in inorganic pigments. The cell is therefore a control.
control.reference_method: Hexavalent chromium by alkaline extraction and IC-ICP-MS or an equivalent validated speciation method (EPA 3060A-type digestion), run on every lot alongside the mandatory total-chromium screen. Cr(VI) cannot exceed total chromium by identity. Escalation: any Cr(VI) result above the method reporting limit triggers pigment and raw-material traceback and CAPA; a result at or above 500 ug/kg — cited here as the EU tattoo-mixture escalation reference and expressly NOT as this row's ceiling — is a hard stop pending root-cause closure.

dusting-talc-powders-adult.name: Dusting/talc powders (adult)
dusting-talc-powders-adult.native_basis: finished leave-on cosmetic as placed on market — total heavy-metal content per unit mass of the product as sold (ug/kg). Total content, not a migration or leachate value, and not a dietary basis. No reconstitution, dilution, or in-use concentration conversion is applied: the ceiling is compared to the product in the form the consumer buys it.
dusting-talc-powders-adult.native_basis_label: Finished leave-on cosmetic, TOTAL CONTENT as placed on market (ug/kg of product as sold), on the technically-unavoidable-impurity basis every instrument in this family uses. Not a migration/leachate basis, not a dietary basis, not an ingredient purity specification.
dusting-talc-powders-adult.scope_note: In scope: adult body, foot and after-bath dusting powders on a talc or other mineral base (talc, kaolin, bentonite, silica, mica), loose or pressed. Out of scope: children's and infant powders, which route to Category 2, and make-up face powders, which route to the makeup row. The form-specific instruments were checked and are all LOOSER than the general cosmetic tier: the EAEU natural-mineral-raw-material tier (lead and arsenic 5000 ug/kg, mercury 1000) applies to this form because the mineral base exceeds one percent; the Korean clay-powder tier (lead 50000) is written for powders using clay as a raw material and does not reach a talc base in any event; the India IS 3959:2004 skin-powder rows (lead 20000, ECO Mark 10000) are finished-product rows for this exact form. Because the general German tier is stricter than every form-specific instrument, it binds. Asbestiform mineral contamination of talc is a separate hazard governed by separate mandatory talc requirements and is outside this eleven-analyte metals panel; nothing in this row should be read as clearing a talc base for asbestos. Sri Lanka SLS 187:2025, the only children's skin-powder tier in the register, carries draft status and is gated out. Colour-additive and ingredient purity specifications are excluded by the basis guard, not merely unused.
dusting-talc-powders-adult.cross_reference: Clean sibling of dusting-powder-cornstarch-adult (row 18), which binds identically because no sovereign instrument splits a talc base from a starch base for metals. Children's and infant dusting powders route to Category 2.

dusting-talc-powders-adult.basis_guard_note: Every named anchor must sit on a FINISHED-COSMETIC (or finished topical product) total-content basis. The guard refuses two families outright. (1) Colour-additive and ingredient purity specifications: the US 21 CFR 73/74 rows, the New Zealand HSR002552 and Singapore ACD carbon-black colourant profiles, the India Cosmetics Rules permitted-colour specification and the Brazil ANVISA RDC 628/2022 organic-colorant specification all bound the purity of ONE raw material, not the maximum for the finished product. Anchoring a finished-product ceiling on a raw-material purity spec is a basis conflation and would be an audit blocker; each of them is also looser than the value that binds here. (2) The EU REACH tattoo and permanent-make-up mixture basis, which is an intradermally introduced mixture and belongs only to the tattoo-inks row. Dietary maximum levels and article migration/extraction limits fail the guard for the same reason.

Pb.label: the Washington Toxic-Free Cosmetics Act finished-cosmetic lead cap (RCW 70A.560.020, 1 ppm = 1000 ug/kg, including impurity lead), the strictest applicable sovereign finished-cosmetic lead maximum; the German BVL 2017 general-cosmetic value (2000) is retained as a disclosed looser candidate

Pb.substantiation: Every form-specific sovereign instrument for this product form was surveyed and named so the derivation shows they were considered rather than missed: India IS 3959:2004 skin powders, 20000 ug/kg, and its ECO Mark tier, 10000; the EAEU TR CU 009/2011 natural-plant-or-mineral-raw-material tier, 5000, which does reach a talc base. A mineral-base dusting powder is not one of the make-up categories the German table lists at 5000, so the general branch is the applicable cell. No colour-additive or ingredient purity specification is used as an anchor: the US 21 CFR 73/74 cosmetic-use specifications (10000-20000 ug/kg), the India permitted-colour specification (20000), the Brazil ANVISA RDC 628/2022 organic-colorant specification (20000) and the New Zealand / Singapore carbon-black colourant profiles (10000) bound one raw material's purity rather than the finished product, they are refused by this row's basis guard, and every one of them is looser than the binding value in any event.

tAs.label: Strictest applicable sovereign total-arsenic maximum for a mineral-base adult dusting powder: Germany BVL 2017 general cosmetic orientation value, 500 ug/kg.

This row is MIXED against the Korean product classes: body, leg, face and theatrical painting products sit inside the colour-makeup class at 30000 ug/kg, while make-up bases, primers, setting sprays and fixatives are not colour products and take the 'other cosmetics' branch at 10000. control.rationale: No jurisdiction publishes a tin maximum for a finished cosmetic. control.rationale: No jurisdiction publishes an aluminium maximum for a finished cosmetic. Ni.label: Korea MFDS 'other cosmetics' nickel tier, 10000 ug/kg — the strictest branch applicable to any form in this mixed-membership row.
Ni.basis_label: Finished cosmetic total content as placed on market (ug/kg of product as sold); technically-unavoidable-impurity basis. Not migration, not leachate, not dietary, not an ingredient purity specification.
Ni.substantiation: Korea MFDS is the ONLY authority in the register that publishes a nickel maximum for a finished cosmetic, and the instrument tiers it by product class: eye makeup 35000 ug/kg, colour makeup 30000, all other cosmetics 10000. Method step 4 requires the government's own product-form split to be preserved, so the applicable branch is selected rather than the strictest branch overall. Both register transpositions of the instrument (MFDS Notice 2024-9 and Notice 2025-63) are named and carry identical values, which is the cross-edition check. No other credible authority publishes a cosmetic nickel ceiling: the EU prohibits nickel compounds as intentional cosmetic ingredients under Regulation 1223/2009 Annex II without setting a numeric trace maximum, and Germany's BVL 2017 table covers only lead, cadmium, arsenic, mercury and antimony. This row is MIXED against the Korean product classes: lipstick, liquid lipstick, gloss, stain and lip liner are colour-makeup products at 30000 ug/kg, while uncoloured lip balms, lip oils and lip masks are lip-care rather than colour products and take the 'other cosmetics' branch at 10000. Because one published ceiling has to be protective for every form certified against the row, the row binds at 10000 ug/kg, which is disclosed over-compliance for the colour forms. Lip products are also the one form in this category that is partly ingested, so where the row's membership makes either branch available the stricter one is the defensible one to publish.

control.rationale: No jurisdiction publishes a tin maximum for a finished cosmetic. The register's tin values are dietary maximum levels for canned foods and powdered beverages, and skin-contact-article or food-contact organotin limits — a dietary basis and a migration basis respectively, neither of which can anchor a cosmetic total-content cell — and there is no near-neighbour cosmetic tin cell to read across from. Tin nevertheless enters this category by real routes: tin-oxide pearlescent and nail-lacquer pigments, organotin catalyst and elastomer residues, and tinplate or tin-lined packaging and closures. Escalation: a total-tin result above the SKU's established baseline triggers pigment, packaging and closure traceback and CAPA.

control.rationale: No jurisdiction publishes an aluminium maximum for a finished cosmetic. The register's aluminium values are a food-additive permission (China GB 2760) and a drinking-water guideline, neither of which is a cosmetic total-content basis, and there is no near-neighbour cosmetic aluminium cell to read across from. Aluminium is nonetheless present in this category at high and highly variable levels by design and by mineral origin — alumina and aluminium-hydroxide fillers and substrates, aluminium-lake pigments, kaolin, bentonite and talc, aluminium powder and aluminium salts — so a single contaminant ceiling would be meaningless while the metal itself cannot go unmeasured. control.rationale: No jurisdiction publishes a total-chromium maximum for a finished cosmetic. control.rationale: No jurisdiction publishes a tin maximum for a finished cosmetic. control.rationale: No jurisdiction publishes an aluminium maximum for a finished cosmetic. control.rationale: No jurisdiction publishes a total-chromium maximum for a finished cosmetic. tattoo-inks.scope_note: In scope: permanent tattoo inks and permanent-make-up pigments, including permanent eyeliner, microblading, scalp micropigmentation, areola and paramedical pigments, together with temporary topical tattoo products — transfer and decal tattoos, henna-style and jagua body art, and airbrush tattoo colours. This row is the one place in Category 13 where the exposure route is INTRADERMAL rather than dermal, and it is governed by a distinct instrument family: EU REACH Annex XVII entry 75 with its Appendix 13 concentration limits, which apply to a mixture placed into the dermis rather than onto the stratum corneum. Because the taxonomy row also carries the temporary topical forms, which are cosmetics rather than intradermal mixtures and are not covered by the REACH entry, each cell names both the applicable REACH value and the applicable finished-cosmetic value and binds at the strictest of them. Ni.label: Korea MFDS 'eye makeup products' nickel tier, 35000 ug/kg — the branch of the only cosmetic nickel instrument that the government itself writes for this product class.
Ni.basis_label: Finished cosmetic total content as placed on market (ug/kg of product as sold); technically-unavoidable-impurity basis. Not migration, not leachate, not dietary, not an ingredient purity specification.
Ni.substantiation: Korea MFDS is the ONLY authority in the register that publishes a nickel maximum for a finished cosmetic, and the instrument tiers it by product class: eye makeup 35000 ug/kg, colour makeup 30000, all other cosmetics 10000. Method step 4 requires the government's own product-form split to be preserved, so the applicable branch is selected rather than the strictest branch overall. Both register transpositions of the instrument (MFDS Notice 2024-9 and Notice 2025-63) are named and carry identical values, which is the cross-edition check. No other credible authority publishes a cosmetic nickel ceiling: the EU prohibits nickel compounds as intentional cosmetic ingredients under Regulation 1223/2009 Annex II without setting a numeric trace maximum, and Germany's BVL 2017 table covers only lead, cadmium, arsenic, mercury and antimony. Every form in this row — kohl, kajal, surma, kaajal, al-kahl and tiro, in powder, paste, stick and pencil form — is an eye cosmetic applied to the lid margin, so all of them sit inside the Korean eye-makeup product class and the 35000 ug/kg branch is the government's own value for this row; the 10000 'other cosmetics' branch and the 30000 colour-makeup branch are both expressly inapplicable by their own scope text. The compiler's stricter-unselected audit surfaces both and this substantiation is the record of why. The asymmetry is stated plainly rather than left for an auditor to find: this row carries the LOOSEST nickel ceiling in Category 13 while being the most heavily contaminated product class in it, because the Korean government wrote its loosest nickel branch for exactly this product form. Method v2.0 retires precautionary numeric overrides, so HMTc publishes the government value; a tighter nickel value for this row has to come from the post-publication certified-lot ratchet under Governance Policy section 12.

control.rationale: No jurisdiction publishes a tin maximum for a finished cosmetic. The register's tin values are dietary maximum levels for canned foods and powdered beverages, and skin-contact-article or food-contact organotin limits — a dietary basis and a migration basis respectively, neither of which can anchor a cosmetic total-content cell — and there is no near-neighbour cosmetic tin cell to read across from. Tin nevertheless enters this category by real routes: tin-oxide pearlescent and nail-lacquer pigments, organotin catalyst and elastomer residues, and tinplate or tin-lined packaging and closures. Testing is therefore mandatory and no ceiling is invented.
control.reference_method: Total tin by ICP-MS after microwave acid digestion, every lot, with organotin speciation by GC-ICP-MS wherever a tin-bearing pigment, catalyst or elastomer component is declared or a tin-lined pack is used. Escalation: a total-tin result above the SKU's established baseline triggers pigment, packaging and closure traceback and CAPA.

control.rationale: No jurisdiction publishes an aluminium maximum for a finished cosmetic. The register's aluminium values are a food-additive permission (China GB 2760) and a drinking-water guideline, neither of which is a cosmetic total-content basis, and there is no near-neighbour cosmetic aluminium cell to read across from. Aluminium is nonetheless present in this category at high and highly variable levels by design and by mineral origin — alumina and aluminium-hydroxide fillers and substrates, aluminium-lake pigments, kaolin, bentonite and talc, aluminium powder and aluminium salts — so a single contaminant ceiling would be meaningless while the metal itself cannot go unmeasured. Testing is therefore mandatory and no ceiling is invented.

Escalation: an aluminium result that the declared formulation cannot account for triggers raw-material traceback and CAPA, because unexplained aluminium indicates an undeclared mineral filler, which is also the most common carrier of the lead, cadmium and arsenic this row does cap.

control.rationale: No jurisdiction publishes a total-chromium maximum for a finished cosmetic. The register's total-chromium values are dietary maximum levels and article limits (toy and stationery coatings, jewellery) in bases that cannot anchor a cosmetic total-content cell, and there is no near-neighbour cosmetic total-chromium cell to read across from. Escalation: unexplained total-chromium elevation triggers pigment and raw-material traceback and CAPA.

control.rationale: No jurisdiction publishes a hexavalent-chromium maximum for a topically applied finished cosmetic. tHg.substantiation: Applicable sovereign maxima surveyed: Germany BVL 2017, 100 ug/kg; US FDA 21 CFR 700.13 (a binding adulteration rule, mercury unavoidable under good manufacturing practice), 1000; China NMPA 2015, 1000; Health Canada, 1000; Taiwan MOHW 2024, 1000; Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63, 1000; Hong Kong Cap. 640, 1000; Singapore HSA 2024 and the ASEAN directive with its transpositions, 1000; Kenya KS 2937:2021, 2000; EAEU TR CU 009/2011 natural-raw-material tier, 1000. The German value binds. subsumed.rationale: MeHg carries no product-specific sovereign cell; it is a component of and bounded by its parent total tHg (MeHg <= tHg), an enforceable ceiling via reflex speciation rather than an empty cell.

Ni.label: Korea MFDS 'other cosmetics' nickel tier, 10000 ug/kg — the strictest branch of the only cosmetic nickel instrument in the register, and the branch that covers this product form.
Ni.basis_label: Finished cosmetic total content as placed on market (ug/kg of product as sold); technically-unavoidable-impurity basis. Not migration, not leachate, not dietary, not an ingredient purity specification.
Ni.substantiation: Korea MFDS is the ONLY authority in the register that publishes a nickel maximum for a finished cosmetic, and the instrument tiers it by product class: eye makeup 35000 ug/kg, colour makeup 30000, all other cosmetics 10000. Method step 4 requires the government's own product-form split to be preserved, so the applicable branch is selected rather than the strictest branch overall. Both register transpositions of the instrument (MFDS Notice 2024-9 and Notice 2025-63) are named and carry identical values, which is the cross-edition check. No other credible authority publishes a cosmetic nickel ceiling: the EU prohibits nickel compounds as intentional cosmetic ingredients under Regulation 1223/2009 Annex II without setting a numeric trace maximum, and Germany's BVL 2017 table covers only lead, cadmium, arsenic, mercury and antimony. This row is neither an eye-makeup nor a colour-makeup product, so the 10000 ug/kg branch is the applicable cell and it binds. Where the mapping of an HMTc row onto the Korean product classes is not unambiguous, or where a row's forms straddle two branches, HMTc takes the stricter branch rather than claiming the looser one.

control.rationale: No jurisdiction publishes a tin maximum for a finished cosmetic. The register's tin values are dietary maximum levels for canned foods and powdered beverages, and skin-contact-article or food-contact organotin limits — a dietary basis and a migration basis respectively, neither of which can anchor a cosmetic total-content cell — and there is no near-neighbour cosmetic tin cell to read across from. Tin nevertheless enters this category by real routes: tin-oxide pearlescent and nail-lacquer pigments, organotin catalyst and elastomer residues, and tinplate or tin-lined packaging and closures. Testing is therefore mandatory and no ceiling is invented.
control.reference_method: Total tin by ICP-MS after microwave acid digestion, every lot, with organotin speciation by GC-ICP-MS wherever a tin-bearing pigment, catalyst or elastomer component is declared or a tin-lined pack is used. Escalation: a total-tin result above the SKU's established baseline triggers pigment, packaging and closure traceback and CAPA.

control.rationale: No jurisdiction publishes an aluminium maximum for a finished cosmetic. The register's aluminium values are a food-additive permission (China GB 2760) and a drinking-water guideline, neither of which is a cosmetic total-content basis, and there is no near-neighbour cosmetic aluminium cell to read across from. Aluminium is nonetheless present in this category at high and highly variable levels by design and by mineral origin — alumina and aluminium-hydroxide fillers and substrates, aluminium-lake pigments, kaolin, bentonite and talc, aluminium powder and aluminium salts — so a single contaminant ceiling would be meaningless while the metal itself cannot go unmeasured. Testing is therefore mandatory and no ceiling is invented.
control.reference_method: Total aluminium by ICP-OES or ICP-MS after microwave acid digestion, every lot, reported on the certificate together with the declared aluminium-bearing ingredients so that the measured burden can be reconciled against the formulation. Escalation: an aluminium result that the declared formulation cannot account for triggers raw-material traceback and CAPA, because unexplained aluminium indicates an undeclared mineral filler, which is also the most common carrier of the lead, cadmium and arsenic this row does cap.

control.rationale: No jurisdiction publishes a total-chromium maximum for a finished cosmetic. Escalation: unexplained total-chromium elevation triggers pigment and raw-material traceback and CAPA.

control.rationale: No jurisdiction publishes a hexavalent-chromium maximum for a topically applied finished cosmetic. The remaining sovereign Cr(VI) values in the register are article extraction limits for textiles and leather, a migration basis that cannot anchor a total-content cell. A not-material determination is NOT available here: Cr(VI) in a pigmented cosmetic matrix is not a method artifact, and the EU legislated a Cr(VI) limit for tattoo mixtures precisely because the species occurs in inorganic pigments. The cell is therefore a control.

Escalation: any Cr(VI) result above the method reporting limit triggers pigment and raw-material traceback and CAPA; a result at or above 500 ug/kg — cited here as the EU tattoo-mixture escalation reference and expressly NOT as this row's ceiling — is a hard stop pending root-cause closure.

antiperspirant.name: Antiperspirant (Al-salt, dirty sibling of r9 deodorant)
antiperspirant.native_basis: finished leave-on cosmetic as placed on market — total heavy-metal content per unit mass of the product as sold (ug/kg). Total content, not a migration or leachate value, and not a dietary basis. No reconstitution, dilution, or in-use concentration conversion is applied: the ceiling is compared to the product in the form the consumer buys it.
antiperspirant.native_basis_label: Finished leave-on cosmetic, TOTAL CONTENT as placed on market (ug/kg of product as sold), on the technically-unavoidable-impurity basis every instrument in this family uses. Not a migration/leachate basis, not a dietary basis, not an ingredient purity specification.
antiperspirant.scope_note: In scope: antiperspirants whose odour and wetness control relies on an aluminium-salt active — aluminium chlorohydrate, aluminium chloride, aluminium sesquichlorohydrate, aluminium zirconium tetrachlorohydrex glycine and the related complexes — in stick, roll-on, cream, gel, soft-solid, spray and wipe forms. Out of scope: aluminium-free deodorants (row 9). Regulatory framing this row has to state plainly: in the European Union and most markets an antiperspirant is a cosmetic under Regulation 1223/2009 and the German BVL orientation values apply to it as a finished cosmetic, which is the basis this row uses; in the United States an antiperspirant is an over-the-counter drug under the 21 CFR 350 monograph, which specifies the permitted aluminium actives and their concentrations but sets no finished-product heavy-metal contaminant ceiling. Neither framing supplies an aluminium contaminant maximum, and this row does not invent one. The contamination question for this form is not how much aluminium is present, which is a label claim, but what travels with a mineral-derived aluminium salt: bauxite- and alum-derived actives carry lead, arsenic and thallium, and that burden is caught by the lead, cadmium, arsenic and mercury cells on this row, all of which apply to the finished product including its percent-level active. Pressurised and airbrush forms: the ceiling applies to the product as placed on market, i.e. the contents of the container including propellant, tested as dispensed. A concentrate-basis laboratory result is never compared to an as-placed-on-market ceiling; where only the concentrate was analysed the basis is recorded and the lot is retested as dispensed. No invented concentrate-to-as-packed conversion factor is used anywhere in this category.
antiperspirant.cross_reference: Clean sibling is deodorants (row 9), where aluminium is a control because there is no aluminium active.
antiperspirant.basis_guard: ^(?!.*(color additive ingredient specification|colou?rant impurity|colourant impurity profile|colorant impurity))(?=.*(cosmetic|finished topical product)).*
antiperspirant.basis_guard_note: Every named anchor must sit on a FINISHED-COSMETIC (or finished topical product) total-content basis. The guard refuses two families outright. (1) Colour-additive and ingredient purity specifications: the US 21 CFR 73/74 rows, the New Zealand HSR002552 and Singapore ACD carbon-black colourant profiles, the India Cosmetics Rules permitted-colour specification and the Brazil ANVISA RDC 628/2022 organic-colorant specification all bound the purity of ONE raw material, not the maximum for the finished product. Anchoring a finished-product ceiling on a raw-material purity spec is a basis conflation and would be an audit blocker; each of them is also looser than the value that binds here. (2) The EU REACH tattoo and permanent-make-up mixture basis, which is an intradermally introduced mixture and belongs only to the tattoo-inks row. Dietary maximum levels and article migration/extraction limits fail the guard for the same reason.

Pb.label: Strictest applicable sovereign lead maximum for a finished cosmetic: Germany BVL 2017 general cosmetic orientation value, 2000 ug/kg.
Pb.basis_label: Finished cosmetic total content as placed on market (ug/kg of product as sold); technically-unavoidable-impurity basis. Not migration, not leachate, not dietary, not an ingredient purity specification.
Pb.substantiation: Applicable sovereign maxima surveyed for this exact form: Germany BVL 2017 general cosmetic orientation value, 2000 ug/kg; China NMPA 2015, 10000; Health Canada, 10000; Taiwan MOHW 2024, 10000; Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63, 20000; Singapore HSA 2024 and the ASEAN directive with its Indonesian and Malaysian transpositions, 20000; Kenya KS 2937:2021, 20000. Looser and therefore non-binding: the EAEU natural-raw-material tier (5000), the Korean clay-powder tier (50000), the India IS 3959:2004 skin-powder rows (20000 and 10000) and the Australian customs value (250000). The German value binds. Its own scope excludes the make-up categories the same table lists at 5000 ug/kg (make-up powder, rouge, eye shadow, eyeliner, kajal and theatrical make-up); none of those forms falls in this row, so the general branch is the applicable cell. The US FDA draft lead guidance for lip and externally applied cosmetics (10000) carries draft status in the register, is gated out by the compiler, and is looser in any case. No colour-additive or ingredient purity specification is used as an anchor: the US 21 CFR 73/74 cosmetic-use specifications (10000-20000 ug/kg), the India permitted-colour specification (20000), the Brazil ANVISA RDC 628/2022 organic-colorant specification (20000) and the New Zealand / Singapore carbon-black colourant profiles (10000) bound one raw material's purity rather than the finished product, they are refused by this row's basis guard, and every one of them is looser than the binding value in any event.

Cd.label: Strictest applicable sovereign cadmium maximum for a finished cosmetic: Germany BVL 2017 general cosmetic orientation value, 100 ug/kg.
Cd.basis_label: Finished cosmetic total content as placed on market (ug/kg of product as sold); technically-unavoidable-impurity basis. Not migration, not leachate, not dietary, not an ingredient purity specification.
Cd.substantiation: Applicable sovereign maxima surveyed for a finished cosmetic: Germany BVL 2017, 100 ug/kg; Thailand (ASEAN transposition), 3000; Health Canada, 3000; China NMPA 2015, 5000; Taiwan MOHW 2024, 5000; Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63, 5000; Singapore HSA 2024 and the ASEAN directive with its Indonesian and Malaysian transpositions, 5000. Germany writes NO formulation split for cadmium — unlike lead and arsenic, where the same table raises the value for named make-up categories — so the 100 ug/kg value applies to every product form in this category without exception. Sri Lanka SLS 187:2025 (children's skin powder, 3000) carries draft status in the register and is gated out by the compiler.

tAs.label: Strictest applicable sovereign total-arsenic maximum for a finished cosmetic: Germany BVL 2017 general cosmetic orientation value, 500 ug/kg.
tAs.basis_label: Finished cosmetic total content as placed on market (ug/kg of product as sold); technically-unavoidable-impurity basis. Not migration, not leachate, not dietary, not an ingredient purity specification.
tAs.substantiation: Applicable sovereign maxima surveyed: Germany BVL 2017 general cosmetic value, 500 ug/kg; China NMPA 2015, 2000; Kenya KS 2937:2021, 2000; Health Canada, 3000; Taiwan MOHW 2024, 3000; Singapore HSA 2024 and the ASEAN directive with its transpositions, 5000; EAEU natural-raw-material tier, 5000; Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63, 10000. The German value binds. The only arsenic split the German table writes raises the value to 2500 ug/kg for theatre, fan and carnival make-up, which does not reach this row. The arsenic cells in this instrument family are TOTAL arsenic; no jurisdiction publishes an inorganic-arsenic maximum for a cosmetic, which is why the iAs cell on this row is a control bounded by this total-arsenic ceiling rather than a number.

subsumed.rationale: iAs carries no product-specific sovereign cell; it is a component of and bounded by its parent total tAs (iAs <= tAs), an enforceable ceiling via reflex speciation rather than an empty cell.

not_material.rationale: Aluminium is the PERMITTED ACTIVE INGREDIENT of an antiperspirant, not a contaminant of it. Escalation: an aluminium result inconsistent with the declared active concentration is a labelling and identity non-conformance referred to CAPA; an aluminium result accompanied by elevated lead or arsenic triggers active-ingredient supplier traceback, because the aluminium is then acting as the carrier.

The two aluminium values the register does carry are a food-additive permission (China GB 2760) and a drinking-water guideline, neither of which is a cosmetic total-content basis or a contaminant maximum for this form.

None publishes an aluminium contaminant maximum for a finished cosmetic.
not_material.substantiation: This is an additive-permitted determination, so high aluminium occurrence is the EXPECTED finding and does not contradict the claim; what would disqualify it is a credible sovereign CONTAMINANT maximum for aluminium in this form, and none exists.
